papers.title: AnySleep: a channel-agnostic deep learning system for high-resolution sleep staging in multi-center cohorts.
papers.abstract: Sleep is essential for health, yet studying its dynamics requires manual sleep staging, a labor-intensive step in research and clinical care. Across centers, polysomnography (PSG) recordings are traditionally scored in 30-s epochs for pragmatic, not physiological, reasons and vary in electrode count, montage, and subject characteristics. These constraints challenge harmonized multi-center studies and the discovery of robust biomarkers on shorter timescales. We present AnySleep, a deep neural network that scores sleep from any electroencephalography (EEG) or electrooculography (EOG) data at adjustable temporal resolutions. We trained and validated the model on over 20,000 overnight recordings (>200,000 h of EEG and EOG) from 28 datasets across multiple clinics to promote robust generalization across sites. The model attains state-of-the-art performance and surpasses or equals established baselines at 30-s epochs. Performance improves with more channels, yet remains strong when EOG is absent, or only EOG or single EEG derivations (frontal, central, or occipital) are available. On sub-30-s timescales, the model captures short wake intrusions consistent with arousals and improves the prediction of pathophysiological conditions (obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy type 1, insomnia) over 30-s scoring. We make the model publicly available to facilitate large-scale studies with heterogeneous electrode setups and accelerate biomarker discovery in sleep.

papers.title: Reduced Locomotor Activity in Juvenile ICR and BALB/c Mice Exposed to Early-Life Sleep Restriction.
papers.abstract: Sleep during early life is essential for normal brain development, and its disruption is implicated as a risk factor for later behavioral abnormalities. We previously reported that chronic postnatal sleep restriction in C57BL/6N mice impairs parvalbumin interneuron development and produces anxiety-like behavior and persistent reductions in locomotor activity into adulthood. Whether these behavioral consequences extend to other genetic backgrounds remains unclear. Here, male ICR (outbred) and BALB/c (inbred) mice underwent daily sleep restriction by gentle handling from postnatal day 8 to 21, and body weight, open-field behavior, and social interaction were assessed thereafter; body weight and open-field behavior were reassessed at 8 weeks of age following return to standard housing. During the juvenile period, sleep restriction reduced total distance traveled in the open field in both strains, without a significant strain × treatment interaction. Significant interactions were found for body weight and time in the central area, both of which were altered in ICR but not in BALB/c mice. In the social interaction test, sleep restriction reduced locomotion and the number of contacts in both strains. At 8 weeks of age, the reduction in total distance traveled remained detectable across strains, and no other measure was affected. BALB/c mice differed from ICR mice in most measures irrespective of treatment. These findings indicate that early-life sleep restriction reduces locomotor activity in both strains, whereas its effects on body weight and central-area exploration were strain-specific. Because sleep was not directly measured and restriction relied on gentle handling, contributions of handling stress cannot be excluded.

papers.title: Environmental enrichment as a multisystem modulator of neurotransmitter function: mechanisms, plasticity, and therapeutic implications.
papers.abstract: Environmental enrichment (EE) has emerged as a powerful non-pharmacological strategy for reshaping brain function through experience dependent plasticity. By integrating sensory, cognitive, motor, and social stimulation, EE provides a biologically relevant framework for understanding how external environments influence neurotransmitter systems that govern mood, cognition, stress adaptation, and neurodegeneration. In this review, we examined the effects of EE on major neurotransmitter pathways, including serotonergic, dopaminergic, glutamatergic, GABAergic, cholinergic, adrenergic, and histaminergic systems. We conducted a structured narrative search of PubMed, supplemented by Google Scholar reference list searching and informed by PRISMA reporting principles. The literature search covered studies published through 4 September 2026. The initial search, completed in February 2025, included 136 articles. A supplemental update screened 108 PubMed records and identified seven additional eligible primary studies, resulting in an updated evidence synthesis comprising 143 articles. Across predominantly preclinical studies, EE was consistently associated with enhanced neurogenesis, synaptic plasticity, stress resilience, and improved behavioral and cognitive outcomes, accompanied by neurotransmitter related changes across multiple brain systems. The most robust evidence supported modulation of serotonergic, dopaminergic, glutamatergic, and GABAergic pathways, whereas adrenergic and histaminergic effects were less well characterized and often indirect. Mechanistically, these effects converged on altered receptor and transporter expression, neurotrophic signaling, CREB dependent transcriptional regulation, and epigenetic remodeling. Collectively, the evidence positions EE as a multisystem regulator of neurotransmitter function with potential relevance to mood disorders, neuroinflammation, neurodegeneration, stroke, addiction, and cognitive decline. Nevertheless, the field remains limited by the predominance of animal data and by substantial heterogeneity in enrichment paradigms. Future translational and clinical studies are needed to define the most effective EE components, timing, and intensity for therapeutic application in humans.

Enrichment was consistently associated with enhanced neurogenesis, synaptic plasticity, stress resilience, and improved behavioral/cognitive outcomes.

papers.title: Decoding Parkinson's disease: a systematic review of qEEG biomarkers across clinical domains.
papers.abstract: This systematic review synthesized evidence on quantitative EEG (qEEG) correlates of Parkinson's disease (PD) across five domains: cognition, motor function, pharmacological interventions, neuromodulation, and sleep/non-motor features, evaluating qEEG's potential as a biomarker across these clinical domains. Following PRISMA, we searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus for studies published from 1991 to 2025. We included studies with ≥10 idiopathic PD patients, resting-state qEEG, and empirical data. Methodological quality was assessed using JBI checklists and AMSTAR. We included 89 studies. Spectral slowing - reduced posterior dominant frequency and increased theta power - was the most consistent correlate of cognitive impairment. Connectivity measures (PLV, graph metrics) showed stronger associations with motor dysfunction, gait impairment, and freezing than spectral power alone. qEEG changed with dopaminergic drugs (increased alpha/beta) and neuromodulation (DBS, tDCS, rTMS, neurofeedback). Sleep studies revealed spindle density reductions linked to dementia risk. qEEG is a promising biomarker for PD, with distinct electrophysiological correlates across cognitive, motor, pharmacological, and neuromodulatory domains. However, methodological standardization is needed before clinical use. With standardized protocols and multicenter validation, qEEG could aid diagnosis, progression tracking, and personalized therapy in PD.

papers.title: An automated EEG-ECG framework for CAP-HRV analysis: enabling brain-heart coupling studies in sleep disorders.
papers.abstract: Multimodal sleep analysis typically requires separate processing pipelines for electroencephalography (EEG) and electrocardiography (ECG), which complicates joint investigation of sleep microstructure and autonomic regulation. Cyclic alternating pattern (CAP) scoring and heart rate variability (HRV) analysis are routinely performed in different software environments, limiting temporal alignment, reproducibility, and scalability. We present an open-source MATLAB framework that integrates rule-based CAP A1 detection and HRV feature extraction within a single, time-synchronized workflow. The pipeline performs standardized EEG and ECG preprocessing, rule-based CAP A1 detection during slow-wave sleep (SWS) implementing the Terzano scoring criteria, R-peak detection via the Pan-Tompkins algorithm, and computation of time-domain, frequency-domain, and nonlinear HRV features by calling the open-source PhysioZoo/mhrv toolbox directly. CAP annotations are aligned with 5-minute ECG epochs through the shared polysomnography (PSG) time base. The complete code is released as an open-source repository to support reuse and extension. Because HRV features are computed by calling the PhysioZoo/mhrv toolbox directly, the pipeline introduces no reimplemented HRV routine and inherits that toolbox's validated feature definitions. CAP A1 detection is provided as a rule-based implementation of published criteria and has not yet been benchmarked against expert manual scoring. A worked example on the OSAD+ subgroup (n = 18) demonstrates pipeline output across CAP and non-CAP epochs, and a healthy-sleep A1-event HRV reference is reported from the public CAP Sleep Database (15 controls, 785 A1 epochs) as a descriptive cross-database reference. The framework provides a reproducible, rule-based, and modular tool for integrated EEG-ECG analysis of sleep microstructure and autonomic dynamics. By enabling synchronized CAP-HRV feature extraction in a single environment, it lowers the engineering barrier to brain-heart coupling research during sleep and provides a foundation for future extensions, including validated CAP detection, a matched-control study, a Python port, and cloud-based deployment.

papers.title: Differential circadian time modulates of dentate gyrus and CA1 excitation-inhibition balance and seizure threshold.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythms regulate seizure threshold and neuronal excitability in epilepsy. Temporal lobe seizures tend to arise more frequently during the diurnal phase relative to the nocturnal phase, yet dentate gyrus (DG) granule cells display elevated intrinsic excitability and CA1 pyramidal neurons show enhanced synaptic excitability at night. Here, we used male adult ICR mice (8-10 weeks old) as experimental subjects. Systemic pilocarpine injection was applied to pharmacologically trigger acute seizures, while AAV (pAAV2/9-CaMKIIα-hChR2 (H134R) - EYFP) delivery followed by optogenetic stimulation (10 Hz, 20 ms pulse width, 5 mW 473 nm blue light) was implemented to evoke region-specific hippocampal seizures. Combining continuous video-electroencephalography (vEEG) recording, optogenetically induced seizure assays, mRNA sequencing, and whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology, we investigated circadian modulation of neuronal excitability and seizure threshold within the DG and CA1 subfields of the hippocampus. Our results revealed divergent circadian regulation of seizure thresholds between the DG and CA1 regions. Notably, the diurnal-nocturnal seizure threshold pattern in CA1 recapitulated that seen in systemic pilocarpien-provoked seizure models. We further confirmed that circadian cycles exert distinct regulatory effects on excitatory/inhibitory synaptic transmission and the intrinsic excitability of hippocampal principal neurons in the DG and CA1. Collectively, this work highlights region-specific circadian control over seizure susceptibility and the brain excitation-inhibition balance. Elucidating circadian influences on hippocampal physiology and seizure threshold will improve the translational value of anti-epileptic therapies and guide time-stratified seizure intervention strategies.

papers.title: Adjunctive Trazodone Effects on Sleep, Mood, and Circulating 5-HT and BDNF in Depression.
papers.abstract: This retrospective study evaluated the association of adjunctive trazodone with sleep architecture, sleep quality, depressive and anxiety symptoms, and circulating 5-HT and BDNF levels in patients with depression. A total of 156 propensity-score-matched patients were included in the final analysis, including 78 who received conventional antidepressant therapy (fluvoxamine monotherapy; control group) and 78 who received combined trazodone and fluvoxamine therapy (observation group). Both treatment regimens were continued for 8 consecutive weeks. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to balance baseline characteristics between the groups. Sleep architecture, sleep quality, depressive and anxiety symptoms, and circulating 5-HT and BDNF levels were assessed at the prespecified clinical time points. Compared with the control group, the observation group demonstrated significantly reduced awake time, prolonged rapid eye movement (REM) sleep and slow-wave sleep (SWS) duration, improved sleep quality, and lower depression and anxiety scores at week 4 (HAMD: 8.23 ± 1.25 vs. 11.88 ± 2.50; HAMA: 4.35 ± 1.32 vs. 7.89 ± 2.17; both P < 0.001), together with higher circulating 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) levels at week 8. Furthermore, the overall clinical response rate was significantly higher in the observation group than in the control group. These findings suggest that adjunctive trazodone was associated with better sleep-related and clinical outcomes, as well as higher circulating 5-HT and BDNF levels, than fluvoxamine monotherapy.

papers.title: Validation of the Telephone MoCA in iRBD and Parkinson's Disease with Conversion to the Standard MoCA.
papers.abstract: Telephone-based cognitive assessment may improve follow-up when face-to-face testing is impractical. The Telephone Montreal Cognitive Assessment (T-MoCA) omits visually dependent items from the standard MoCA, but its validity in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) and Parkinson's disease (PD), remains uncertain. To assess agreement between the T-MoCA and face-to-face MoCA-22 in iRBD and PD, and derive and externally validate a MoCA-22 to MoCA-30 conversion. In the Oxford Parkinson's Disease Centre (OPDC) Discovery Cohort, 137 participants (38 controls, 47 iRBD, 52 PD) completed T-MoCA and MoCA-22 assessments. Agreement was evaluated using Lin's concordance correlation coefficient, Bland-Altman analysis, and equivalence testing with ±1-point bounds. Equipercentile equating with log-linear smoothing was used to derive a MoCA-22 to MoCA-30 conversion using Discovery data (3561 tests), with validation in Tracking Parkinson's (5767 tests) and Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (5047 tests). T-MoCA and face-to-face MoCA-22 scores were statistically equivalent, with minimal bias; 83.3% of scores differed by ≤1 point. However, concordance between test formats was moderate (Lin's CCC = 0.58). Across 14,375 MoCA assessments, equipercentile equating outperformed proportional scaling in development and validation cohorts. Propagating T-MoCA-MoCA-22 variability resulted in wider prediction intervals for T-MoCA-derived MoCA-30 estimates, indicating individual-level uncertainty, with intervals estimable only for T-MoCA scores ≥17 due to sparse data. At group level, T-MoCA is a valid remote measure of non-visual MoCA domains in iRBD and PD. The equating function supports cohort-level harmonization of MoCA-22 and MoCA-30 scores, while individual T-MoCA-derived MoCA-30 estimates should be interpreted with caution.

papers.title: Chronic circadian misalignment in military personnel: a potential contributor to neuroinflammation risk.
papers.abstract: Circadian rhythm disruption is increasingly recognized as a key contributor to neurological disorders; however, its role is often viewed as a secondary consequence rather than a primary driver of brain dysfunction. We argue that chronic circadian misalignment should be reconceptualized as a potential, modifiable contributor to neuroinflammatory risk, rather than viewed solely as a secondary consequence. Military personnel represent a unique and underutilized human model in this context, as they are chronically exposed to predictable circadian stressors, including irregular training schedules, overseas travel, sleep restriction, and pre-operational stress. At the molecular level, circadian misalignment disrupts core clock gene regulation (e.g., CLOCK, BMAL1), leading to downstream alterations in mitochondrial function and redox homeostasis. These changes promote a sustained pro-inflammatory milieu, impair neuroimmune balance, and compromise synaptic plasticity and blood-brain barrier integrity. We propose that these mechanisms collectively increase vulnerability to cognitive dysfunction and mood disturbances, even in otherwise healthy and physically fit populations. Thus, circadian misalignment in military personnel is not merely a byproduct of performance demands, but a biologically plausible contributor to brain dysfunction that warrants targeted intervention and further mechanistic study. Reframing circadian disruption as a potential, modifiable neurobiological risk factor has significant implications for both research and practice.

papers.title: A technical review of dynamic brain functional imaging combined with EEG spectral parameters in the screening of early-stage brain injury.
papers.abstract: Early-stage brain injury encompasses subtypes such as mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI), silent stroke and subclinical brain injury. It is characterised by negative imaging findings, subtle symptoms and a high risk of long-term neurological deficits, presenting a key challenge in the early screening and prevention of neurological diseases. Traditional imaging techniques, such as structural Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Computed Tomography (CT), can only identify organic morphological lesions. Their detection rate for early micro-injuries at the level of neuronal electrophysiology and brain network function is extremely low. Consequently, these techniques struggle to meet the clinical needs for early screening, assessment, and intervention. Electroencephalography (EEG) spectral changes (including conventional spectral slowing and 1/f aperiodic abnormalities) and large-scale dynamic neural network disruption across the entire brain are core pathological features of early brain functional damage; they may serve as indirect correlates of microscopic pathological changes such as an imbalance in neuronal excitation-inhibition and abnormalities in the efficiency of brain information transmission. Based on this, this paper proposes a Dynamic-Spectral Coupling (DSC) framework, which proposes spectral abnormalities as a potential upstream mechanism associated with network reorganisation. Within this framework, this narrative review summarizes dynamic functional magnetic resonance imaging (dynamic fMRI), EEG spectral analysis and multimodal fusion technologies, with a particular focus on elucidating the coupling mechanisms between EEG periodic and 1/f aperiodic spectral parameters and dynamic brain network indicators. The review outlines the screening value and application advantages of multimodal fusion technologies in mTBI, occult cerebrovascular injury and subclinical brain injury. Furthermore, the paper summarises the current limitations of these technologies in terms of clinical translation, methodology and database development. Taking into account the clinical needs of neurorehabilitation, it proposes future development directions, including the development of lightweight devices, AI-assisted diagnosis, the establishment of standardised analytical systems and the translation of precision rehabilitation. The aim is to provide technical guidance and theoretical support for screening, risk stratification and rehabilitation planning in early-stage brain injury, while acknowledging that clinical utility remains to be established.

papers.title: Associations of self-reported physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep duration with mental and behavioral health among civil aviation flight students: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: To examine the associations of self-reported physical activity at different intensities, total sedentary time, and sleep duration with mental and behavioral health indicators among civil aviation flight students. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted at a civil aviation university from January 5 to 30, 2026. A total of 776 students majoring in Flight Technology were included, of whom 774 (99.7%) were male. Because only two participants were female, the primary inferential analyses were restricted to male participants. Physical activity and sedentary behavior were assessed using modified self-report items. Physical activity duration represented participants' self-reported activity time on a typical activity day rather than average daily or weekly physical activity time; sleep exposure was assessed using categorical self-reported sleep duration. Depression, anxiety, stress, and problematic Internet use were assessed using validated scales. Generalized estimating equation models were used to examine cross-sectional associations between the behavioral indicators and outcomes, with false discovery rate (FDR) correction. In the fully adjusted male sample, after FDR correction, longer self-reported vigorous-intensity physical activity duration on a typical activity day was associated with lower anxiety scores; self-reported sleep duration <7 h was associated with higher depression, anxiety, stress, and problematic Internet use scores; and longer self-reported total sedentary time was associated with higher problematic Internet use scores. No statistically significant linear associations were observed between moderate- or light-intensity physical activity and any outcome after FDR correction. The observed associations were generally small: the association between vigorous-intensity physical activity and anxiety was approximately 0.10 outcome standard deviations, the associations between sleep duration <7 h and the corresponding outcomes were approximately 0.24-0.27 standard deviations, and the association between total sedentary time and problematic Internet use was approximately 0.04 standard deviations. The directions of the main associations were generally consistent across multiple sensitivity analyses, although the strength of statistical evidence for some associations varied by outcome definition, sample restriction, and data-processing approach. Among male civil aviation flight students, self-reported physical activity, total sedentary time, and sleep duration were cross-sectionally associated with selected mental and behavioral health indicators. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings cannot establish causality, an optimal physical activity dose, a sleep intervention threshold, or time-substitution effects between behaviors. The findings suggest that behavioral indicators and mental and behavioral health status may be considered jointly in this population, but the observed associations require confirmation in longitudinal studies using objective, device-based behavioral measures.

papers.title: Hair-compatible adhesive hydrogel electrodes for electroencephalography-based cybersickness detection and closed-loop mitigation.
papers.abstract: Cybersickness develops dynamically during virtual reality (VR) exposure, creating a need for continuous electroencephalography (EEG) monitoring. However, wearable EEG remains limited by the difficulty of establishing low-impedance, conformal, and mechanically stable electrode-scalp interfaces on hair-covered skin, especially under sweating and head motion. Here, we report a shell-assisted adhesive hydrogel electrode that combines hair penetration with stable scalp adhesion for rapid EEG acquisition. Poly (3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene)-modified polydopamine particles (PDA/PEDOT) are incorporated into an adhesive hydrogel to achieve high conductivity, strong adhesion, and mechanical compliance while preserving PEDOT conductivity without poly (styrene sulfonate) incorporation or additional treatment. A flexible silicone shell guides the hydrogel through hair, prevents unwanted hydrogel-hair adhesion, and enables intimate scalp contact. The electrode achieves an EEG signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 11.66 dB, while motion-induced interference under sweating is only 22.8% of that observed with traditional wet electrodes. Integrated into a wearable headband, the system detects cybersickness with 92.5% accuracy and enables closed-loop noisy galvanic vestibular stimulation (nGVS), increasing users' tolerance time by 52.3%. This work provides a practical strategy for hair-compatible soft biointerfaces and wearable neurotechnology for immersive human-machine interaction.

papers.title: Automated attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder detection using an explainable EEGNet model based on electroencephalogram signals.
papers.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition where traditional diagnostics often suffer from subjective biases and a lack of objective biomarkers. In this study, we developed a novel, automated, and interpretable diagnostic framework using the specialized EEGNet model to extract spatio-temporal patterns directly from raw EEG signals, ensuring robust ADHD detection and model generalizability across a clinical lifespan ranging from 5 to 89 years. The primary innovation of this research lies in a specialized, lightweight EEGNet model that directly processes raw 5-second spatio-temporal EEG segments, eliminating the need for manual feature engineering or signal-to-image transformation. Our findings demonstrate that EEGNet achieves superior performance, reaching an average accuracy of 89.48% (±4.21%) and an AUC of 0.96 (±0.03), significantly outperforming the transfer learning models. A distinguishing feature of this work is the transition from black-box modeling to explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) by integrating Saliency Maps and SHAP values, which decoded the model's decision-making logic to identify key contributing channels (Fp1, Fp2, C3, T5, and A2) whose spatial attributions align with established neuroscientific literature on ADHD. The high ranking of the Fp1 (prefrontal) channel aligns with established neuroscientific evidence regarding executive dysfunction in ADHD. Furthermore, the implementation of a rigorous inter-subject evaluation demonstrates the preliminary clinical feasibility of this interpretable framework, providing a foundation for future validation on larger multi-center cohorts and offering a robust assistive tool for real-world neurological assessments.

papers.title: A multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset with repeated experience sampling
papers.abstract: The integration of electroencephalography (EEG) and functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) can be used to characterize temporal and spatial components of neural activity during unfolding mental experience. Here we introduce a multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset with measures of continuous behavior and spontaneous mental experience. Data components, organized in Brain Imaging Dataset Structure (BIDS) format, include fMRI, EEG with carbon wire loop sensors for artifact removal, continuous performance task responses, experience sampling ratings, and mental health surveys, from 24 healthy adults. Tasks included the gradual-onset continuous performance task and resting state with intermittent experience sampling of 13 unique thought dimensions (36 repetitions, including 468 total ratings, per participant). The same protocol was completed on two different days, yielding approximately 1.33 hours of simultaneous EEG-fMRI data per individual. The dataset may be used to explore the behavioral and experiential relevance of brain activity during the wakeful resting state. The dataset also provides a means to study the reliability of relationships between fMRI and EEG features across sessions within individuals.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese medicine-related interventions and the cGAS-STING axis in neuroinflammation: disease contexts and mechanisms of action.
papers.abstract: Research on traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)-related interventions has shifted from overall phenotypic effects to defined neuroimmune targets. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) axis connects cytosolic DNA sensing with host defense and sterile inflammatory injury, but the functional direction of this pathway changes with disease context. This review organizes preclinical findings by pathological setting and site of action. It examines herbal formulas and natural compounds, followed by acupuncture, electroacupuncture, and related delivery systems. Several sterile injury models associate benefit with reduced pathway-related inflammation. Acute sleep deprivation provides an example of protection accompanying restored STING signaling. Early herpes simplex virus infection follows a different pattern: restoration of suppressed antiviral signaling improves host defense. In acute postoperative pain and cancer-induced bone pain models, increased STING-IFN-I signaling accompanies electroacupuncture-induced analgesia. Some interventions reduce mitochondrial DNA stimulation. Others act on cGAS or STING, with separate studies targeting STING trafficking. Downstream inflammatory and cell-death responses form the final level. Mechanistic attribution is strongest when genetic or pharmacological perturbation links pathway change to functional outcome; direct binding has been demonstrated for a small group of compounds. These findings support a context-sensitive framework for interpreting modulation direction that requires validation within individual disease models. Clinical translation will depend on reproducible formulation composition, effective brain exposure, and safety.

papers.title: Screen time exposure, sleep alterations, and their relationship with excess weight in children and adolescents.
papers.abstract: The digital era has led to an unprecedented increase in screen time exposure among youth, creating a critical intersection between technology use, sleep hygiene, and metabolic health. To evaluate the association between daily screen time, sleep quality, and the prevalence of overweight and obesity in a pediatric clinical population. A cross-sectional study was conducted on 70 patients (mean age 10.8 years). Subjects were categorized into obese (n = 44) and non-obese (n = 26) groups. Anthropometric data, body composition (perivisceral fat), biochemical parameters [insulin, Homeostasis Model Assessment (HOMA), lipid profile], and lifestyle habits (Krece Plus and KIDMED tests) were analyzed. Binary logistic regression was performed to estimate odds ratios (OR) for obesity and sleep disturbances. Obesity was significantly associated with higher perivisceral fat (P < 0.001), systolic blood pressure (P = 0.009), insulin levels (P = 0.035), and HOMA index (P = 0.024), alongside lower high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (P < 0.001). Sociodemographic analysis revealed that maternal education level was significantly lower in the obese group (P = 0.006). Regarding lifestyle, obese children reported significantly higher daily screen time (2.9 hours vs 2.1 hours; P = 0.047) and shorter sleep duration (8.4 hours vs 9.1 hours; P = 0.021). The prevalence of chronic sleep disturbances was notably higher in obese subjects (39% vs 8.3%; P = 0.016). After adjusting for confounders, screen time was strongly associated with a higher risk of obesity (OR: 3.08; 95%CI: 1.53-7.90) and sleep problems (OR: 1.65; 95%CI: 0.96-2.99). Excessive screen time and poor sleep quality are strongly associated with pediatric obesity and its metabolic comorbidities. Furthermore, lower maternal education level and family history of diabetes are significant compounding factors. Clinical interventions should address digital hygiene and sleep quality as essential pillars in the management of childhood excess weight.

papers.title: Co-exposure to octocrylene and polystyrene nanoplastics induces neuro- and reproductive toxicity in zebrafish: Association with circadian rhythm and HPG axis disruption.
papers.abstract: Octocrylene (OC) is a widely used ultraviolet filter frequently detected in aquatic environments. Micro- and nanoplastics (M/NPs) are persistent pollutants that can adsorb organic contaminants such as OC, leading to combined exposure risks. However, the long-term neuroendocrine effects of environmentally relevant co-exposure to OC and nanoplastics remain poorly understood. In this study, adult zebrafish were exposed to OC (5 µg/L) with or without polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs, 80 nm, 1.0 mg/L) for 28 days. Co-exposure to OC and PS-NPs significantly disrupted behavioral phenotypes, suppressed bdnf transcription, and downregulated core circadian clock genes (per1b, per2, per3, cry1a, cry2, nr1d1), indicating aggravated neurotoxicity. Furthermore, co-exposure interfered with sex hormone synthesis and caused gonadal damage by modulating the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis at the transcriptional level, leading to more severe reproductive toxicity and impaired offspring development. Molecular docking revealed that OC may directly interact with estrogen receptors (ERα, ERβ) and CYP19, providing a molecular basis for endocrine disruption. These findings demonstrate that PS-NPs enhance the neurotoxic and reproductive effects of OC through circadian and HPG axis disruption, highlighting the need for considering nanoplastics as toxicity amplifiers in environmental risk assessment.

papers.title: Associations of circadian clock genes with the risk of depression in adults with sleep disturbances: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Depression, influenced by both genetic and environmental factors, is often accompanied by sleep disturbances. However, studies examining the associations between circadian clock genes, depression, and sleep disturbances have yielded inconsistent findings. This study investigated the associations of circadian clock genes with depression in adults with sleep disturbances. A systematic search of six databases (EBSCOhost, Medline, Scopus, Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science) was conducted for articles published up to July 10, 2025. The study was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42023472328). A total of 23 studies examining depression in adults with sleep disturbances were included. Eight genes (CLOCK, NR1D, TIM, CRY, PER2, PER3, ARNTL, and CSNK1) were associated with depression in adults with sleep disturbances, while RORA showed no significant association. CRY showed the numerically highest pooled odds ratio for depression in adults with sleep disturbances (OR= 1.6, 95% CI: 1.4-1.8, p < 0.01), although its confidence interval overlapped with those of several other genes. These findings underscore the role of circadian genes and suggest further gene identification may clarify depression and sleep disturbance pathways.

papers.title: Impact of nocturnal oxygen saturation on sleep quality and exercise performance in adult Fontan patients.
papers.abstract: A decreased peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) is common in Fontan patients. We aimed to determine whether these patients experience greater nocturnal desaturation (ΔSpO2,noct), and to which extent this may impact sleep quality and exercise performance, compared to healthy controls. 16 adult Fontan patients and 16 healthy, individually matched controls completed questionnaires on quality of life, sleep quality, and daytime sleepiness, performed measurements of lung function and diffusion capacity (DLCO), and cycled in a cardiopulmonary exercise test to volitional exhaustion. Sleep quality was assessed with a wrist-worn actigraph and nocturnal SpO2 was measured with a pulse oximeter during six nights. Fontan patients experienced greater ΔSpO2,noct (-3.4 ± 0.8%-points, n = 14) compared to their controls (-2.5 ± 0.6%-points, n = 14, p = 0.001). In patients, ΔSpO2,noct correlated with baseline SpO2, DLCO, and exercise performance. Fontan patients had a longer sleep onset latency (22.8 ± 9.6 vs. 10.8 ± 6.0 min, p < 0.001) and lower self-perceived physical functioning (91 ± 7 vs. 100 ± 0 points, p < 0.001), but similar subjective sleep quality (4.2 ± 1.5 vs. 3.4 ± 1.4 points, p = 0.121) and daytime sleepiness (6.1 ± 4.3 vs. 6.3 ± 2.8 points, p = 0.884) compared to controls. In patients, daytime sleepiness correlated with the total number of desaturation events (r = 0.74, p = 0.003). Indices of nocturnal SpO2 were related to daytime sleepiness and reduced exercise performance, and may therefore be a contributing factor to exercise limitation in adult Fontan patients. Enhancing nocturnal SpO2 may thus be a promising target to improve daytime sleepiness and exercise performance in adult Fontan patients.

papers.title: Gray matter alterations and their atlas-based spatial associations with neurotransmitter distributions in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.abstract: Multiple neurotransmitter systems are implicated in the pathophysiology of isolated rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) and its progression to α-synucleinopathy. This study aimed to identify baseline gray matter (GM) alterations in patients with iRBD compared with healthy controls and to examine their spatial correspondence with known neurotransmitter distributions. We further characterized GM patterns associated with future phenoconversion and their neurochemical context. A total of 109 patients with iRBD who completed at least one follow-up evaluation and 24 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent structural magnetic resonance imaging. Gray matter volume (GMV) alterations were assessed using the CAT12 toolbox. Spatial correlations between group-level GMV difference maps and neurotransmitter atlases were evaluated using the JuSpace toolbox. At baseline, patients with iRBD showed reduced GMV in the right cerebellar cortex and vermis, along with increased GMV in the left putamen and pallidum. These GMV alterations demonstrated significant spatial correspondence with dopaminergic receptor and transporter maps, including dopamine D2 receptors and the dopamine transporter (DAT). Among patients with iRBD, those who subsequently phenoconverted exhibited lower baseline GMV in the right medial orbital gyrus compared with non-converters. This pattern showed significant spatial correlations with serotonergic (5-HT2A), glutamatergic (mGluR5), GABAergic (GABAa), and dopaminergic (FDOPA) neurotransmitter maps. Patients with iRBD exhibit distinct patterns of GMV alteration that spatially align with dopaminergic neurotransmitter distribution maps, while phenoconversion is associated with GM changes corresponding to multiple neurotransmitter systems, although the phenoconversion findings are exploratory.

papers.title: Preoperative Sleep Modulation with Melatonin and Zolpidem and Its Impact on Postoperative Pain and Recovery: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Perioperative sleep disturbances and anxiety may worsen postoperative pain, increase opioid consumption, and delay recovery. Melatonin and zolpidem improve sleep, but their effects on postoperative pain remain incompletely characterized. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched for studies published between 2000 and 2025 investigating preoperative melatonin or zolpidem in surgical patients. Two reviewers independently screened records using Rayyan, resolving discrepancies through consensus. Of 404 records identified, 119 duplicates were removed. Of 285 screened records, 269 were excluded, leaving 16 articles for inclusion. Melatonin demonstrated anxiolytic, analgesic, and chronobiotic effects. It reduced salivary cortisol, modulated stress responses, attenuated proinflammatory pathways, and supported circadian recovery, particularly in patients with preoperative anxiety. Its analgesic efficacy was comparable to clonidine in some trials, with a favorable safety profile. Zolpidem improved preoperative sleep quality and reduced postoperative pain and opioid consumption, potentially through improved sleep architecture. In colorectal surgery, zolpidem also reduced tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α). Melatonin demonstrated more consistent effects on cortisol, suggesting distinct physiological mechanisms. Melatonin and zolpidem offer complementary perioperative benefits. Melatonin may provide broader neuroendocrine and analgesic effects, whereas zolpidem may benefit patients with insomnia. Larger trials are needed to optimize dosing and patient selection.

papers.title: Insomnia and medication overuse headache: neurobiological links, reciprocal interactions, and integrated therapeutic strategies.
papers.abstract: Medication overuse headache (MOH) and insomnia are not merely coincidental companions: each measurably worsens the severity and treatment response of the other. Whether this association reflects a genuine reciprocal influence, a shared constitutional vulnerability, or some combination of both carries direct practical consequences for clinical decision-making. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from Mendelian randomization genetics, polysomnographic cohort studies, pharmacological withdrawal trials, and mechanistic neurobiology, based on a search of PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar through 20 June 2026. Genetic analyses are compatible with a directional association between insomnia liability and migraine risk, although causation is not established and the instruments capture migraine broadly rather than the MOH phenotype, a limitation that applies to all causal inferences in this review. In the other direction, opioids, barbiturates, and triptans each disrupt sleep architecture through mechanisms specific to their molecular targets, and questionnaire-based withdrawal studies consistently report parallel improvements in sleep quality and headache frequency. Three neurobiological substrates appear centrally involved: orexinergic dysregulation, melatonin suppression, and glial neuroinflammation. Together, they may sustain a self-reinforcing cycle that neither detoxification alone nor sleep treatment alone can fully dismantle. The COMISA phenotype (comorbid insomnia and obstructive sleep apnea) and concurrent psychiatric illness compound treatment resistance and raise relapse rates at one year. Objective polysomnographic evidence that sleep architecture actually recovers after drug withdrawal is absent from the literature - a gap that limits the mechanistic conclusions that can be drawn. The available evidence is consistent with the hypothesis that concurrent medication withdrawal, CBT-I, preventive pharmacotherapy - including anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies - and CPAP where indicated may yield better outcomes than sequential management, but this hypothesis has not been tested in a randomized controlled trial. Designing that trial is the most pressing research need in this field.

papers.title: Cortical traveling wave analysis reveals weaker resting forward theta waves and greater task-related modulation in obsessive compulsive disorder.
papers.abstract: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is associated with abnormalities in large-scale brain network dynamics. Conventional electroencephalography (EEG) captures local oscillatory activity but does not characterize spatiotemporal propagation patterns. This study investigates cortical traveling waves, which index directional information flow across the cortex, to determine whether they provide novel insights into altered neural communication in OCD. Resting-state (eyes-closed) and task-based (Go/NoGo, Flanker) EEG were recorded from 25 individuals with OCD and 27 healthy controls (HCs). Traveling waves were quantified along midline electrodes using two-dimensional Fast Fourier Transforms to extract forward (posterior-to-anterior) and backward (anterior-to-posterior) propagation in theta (4-8Hz) and alpha (8-13Hz) bands. Group differences were assessed using Bayesian and frequentist linear mixed-effects models controlling for age and sex. At rest, a significant group-by-direction interaction was observed in the theta band (P = 0.0006), driven by weaker forward traveling wave strength in OCD relative to HC. No group differences were observed for backward waves or in the alpha band. During the Flanker task, the OCD group showed a significantly greater increase in forward theta wave strength from rest than HC (P = 0.022). No associations were found between traveling wave measures and symptom severity. OCD is characterized by altered theta-band traveling wave dynamics, specifically reduced forward (bottom-up) signaling at rest, and increased task-related modulation during the Flanker task. These findings suggest disrupted hierarchical cortical communication and inefficient engagement of sensory-driven processes. The absence of symptom correlations suggests a potential trait-like neurophysiological marker or endophenotype of OCD.

papers.title: Unleashing children's potential: An evidence-based narrative review of strategies to enhance cognitive function and intelligence in school-age children.
papers.abstract: School-age cognitive development (6-12 years) represents a critical window of neural plasticity, during which intelligence and executive function can be meaningfully enhanced. Once considered largely fixed, these cognitive capacities are now recognized as dynamic, multifactorial, and modifiable through environmental, nutritional, educational, and psychosocial interventions. This review synthesizes current evidence on strategies to optimize cognitive function in typically developing children as well as special populations, including those with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, learning disabilities, twice exceptional profiles, or socio-economic disadvantage. We examine the impact of macronutrient and micronutrient intake, gut-brain interactions, physical activity, sleep quality, parenting practices, stress regulation, educational curricula, digital learning tools, mindfulness, and social-emotional learning, highlighting mechanistic pathways, intervention effectiveness, and population-specific considerations. Methodological challenges, including heterogeneity, cultural bias, and translational gaps, are critically appraised. Finally, we propose priorities for multimodal, personalized, and scalable interventions, informed by perspectives from precision education, implementation science, and longitudinal research. By integrating neuroscientific, educational, and psychosocial insights, this review provides actionable recommendations for clinicians, educators, and policymakers to maximize children's cognitive potential, academic achievement, and long-term adaptive outcomes.

papers.title: Circadian rhythm dysregulation and ferroptosis in hypertension: mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
papers.abstract: Hypertension exhibits a pronounced circadian rhythm; however, the mechanisms by which circadian disruption translates temporal imbalance into sustained vascular and renal injury remain unclear. Increasing evidence suggests that circadian misalignment may promote endothelial dysfunction, vascular remodeling, and renal injury through ferroptosis driven by oxidative stress dysregulation, thereby increasing the risk of hypertension. Based on current evidence, this review proposes that circadian disruption induces a temporal mismatch between oxidative stress generation and antioxidant defense, thereby lowering the threshold for ferroptosis in cardiovascular and renal tissues. This process may amplify hemodynamic stress, impair endothelial integrity, and disturb renal sodium handling, ultimately contributing to the development and progression of hypertension. Although direct causal evidence remains limited, this review integrates circadian biology with ferroptosis and provides a mechanistic link between time-dependent physiological regulation and structural organ damage, highlighting a potentially promising strategy for future hypertension intervention.

papers.title: Case Report: Electroencephalography-informed low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting the supplementary motor area in severe functional movement disorder.
papers.abstract: Functional movement disorder (FMD) is increasingly being recognized as a condition associated with abnormal brain network connectivity; however, effective treatment strategies remain limited. We report the case of a patient with severe FMD that developed following an occupational injury and was characterized by functional tremors accompanied by migraines and prominent autonomic symptoms. Based on electroencephalography (EEG) network analysis, low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation targeting the supplementary motor area was administered, followed by staged rehabilitation incorporating visual feedback. The combined intervention reduced tremors and improved gait speed, activities of daily living, and EEG network connectivity. This case highlights the potential utility of combining EEG-guided neuromodulation with staged rehabilitation for the treatment of FMD and supports further investigation of this approach.

papers.title: Sleep disturbance in inflammatory bowel disease: clinical associations and gaps in care.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbance is highly prevalent in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), affecting up to 70% of patients with active disease and 40% in remission, and is associated with worse clinical and patient-reported outcomes. Understanding of the multifactorial drivers of sleep disturbances in IBD remains limited, and as such, there is an absence of clear guidance for evaluating and managing sleep problems in this population. We aimed to identify factors associated with sleep disturbance and characterize patient beliefs, self-management strategies, and interest in sleep-focused testing and treatments. Adults with Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis completed a cross-sectional survey assessing disease activity, sleep quality, stress, chronotype, fatigue, and mood. A study-specific questionnaire evaluated sleep-related beliefs, behaviors, and treatment interest. Descriptive analyses characterized sleep patterns and behaviors, and multivariable regression identified factors associated with poor sleep. Among 204 participants, 76.5% reported poor sleep quality and 55.9% had clinically significant sleep disturbance, which was more common in active disease than remission (80.9% vs 46.0%, P < .001). Active disease (odds ratio [OR], 4.31), higher perceived stress (OR, 1.21), and anxiety (OR, 2.63) were associated with increased odds of clinically significant sleep disturbance, while intermediate (OR, 0.16) and morning chronotypes (OR, 0.07) were associated with lower odds of clinically significant sleep disturbance compared with evening chronotypes. Most participants reported self-management behaviors related to sleep, with widespread use of sleep hygiene and over-the-counter strategies but minimal exposure to cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (0.5%). Interest in sleep-focused interventions was high, particularly for wearable monitoring, home-based testing, and behavioral and light-based therapies. Sleep disturbance in inflammatory bowel disease is common and reflects interacting inflammatory, psychological, and circadian factors. Use of evidence-based therapies remains extremely limited, highlighting a substantial gap in care.

papers.title: Neurodevelopmental outcomes of infants evaluated for but not treated with therapeutic hypothermia: a prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic hypothermia (TH) is the standard of care for moderate to severe neonatal encephalopathy (NE). Although some centers consider TH for mild NE, neurodevelopmental outcomes of infants who do not meet eligibility criteria are incompletely defined. Infants evaluated for TH based on perinatal risk factors, but who did not meet institutional eligibility criteria, were prospectively enrolled. Neurodevelopmental outcomes were assessed at 24 months. Bayley-4 scores <85 were classified as sub-normative performance. Of 39 infants enrolled, 26 completed Bayley-4 assessments. Thirteen (50%) demonstrated sub-normative performance in at least one developmental domain; only one of them had an acute brain injury on MRI. Compared with infants with average-range performance, those with sub-normative performance had higher postnatal base deficits (10.1 vs 6 mmol/L, p 0.04), higher postnatal lactate levels (9.4 vs 4.9 mmol/L, p 0.05), and a trend toward less sleep-wake cycling on aEEG (45% vs 83%, p 0.06). A substantial proportion of infants evaluated for but not treated with TH demonstrated sub-normative developmental performance at 2 years. Absence of acute MRI-detected injury does not preclude later developmental vulnerability. These findings support longitudinal follow-up of infants who are evaluated for TH but do not meet TH criteria. Infants evaluated for but not treated with therapeutic hypothermia demonstrated a measurable risk of neurodevelopmental vulnerability at 2 years, with 50% demonstrating sub-normative performance (>1 SD below the normative mean) in at least one domain on the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development Fourth Edition. Early postnatal metabolic abnormalities in infants evaluated for therapeutic hypothermia showed a potential association with later developmental outcomes. There is a need for improved risk stratification and structured longitudinal follow-up for infants evaluated for but who do not meet cooling criteria.

papers.title: Almond shells as environmental enrichment for laying hens: Implications for welfare and egg quality.
papers.abstract: Environmental enrichment is a promising strategy to improve welfare in laying hens, particularly in aviary systems where large group sizes and complex social interactions can predispose birds to fearfulness and feather pecking. This study evaluated the effects of providing coarsely milled almond shells (AS; geometric mean diameter = 1525 µm) as an environmental enrichment on welfare indicators, egg quality, and organ development in large commercial aviary flocks. The study compared two treatments-hens receiving AS and a control group that did not receive AS-with four pens per treatment and 2,500 hens per pen. Welfare indicators, as well as external and internal egg quality traits, were assessed at peak lay (13 weeks (wk) of trial; 33 weeks of age) and post-peak lay (23 wk of trial; 43 wk of age). In addition, at 23 wk of trial, serum corticosterone and relative organ weights were measured. At peak lay, hens provided with AS enrichment showed reduced fearfulness in the novel object test (P < 0.001), a trend toward lower gentle feather pecking (P < 0.1), and fewer comb pecking wounds and lower overall pecking scores (P < 0.001). No differences were observed in free feathers in the litter or severe/aggressive pecking. At post-peak, hens provided with AS enrichment continued to show lower fear responses (P < 0.001), fewer free feathers in the litter (P < 0.05), and tendencies toward reduced plumage damage, lower overall pecking scores, and reduced serum corticosterone (7.05 vs. 11.23 ng/mL; P < 0.1). Both internal and external egg quality parameters remained unaffected at both ages. Relative weights of liver, proventriculus, gizzard, pancreas, and spleen were unchanged, while small and large intestines tended to be heavier in hens provided with AS enrichment (P < 0.1). In conclusion, milled AS could be an effective enrichment for aviary-housed laying hens, by reducing fear and stress, mitigating feather pecking, and supporting minor digestive adaptations, without compromising egg quality. These findings support the use of AS as a sustainable agricultural by-product to improve welfare in large commercial flocks.

papers.title: Human iEEG recordings during audiovisual speech violations support and extend predictive routing models
papers.abstract: Rather than constantly reconstructing the world solely through sensory input, predictive processing theories posit that the brain utilizes predictions maintained as internal representations to guide sensory processing. An emerging model, predictive routing, proposes that an interplay between neuronal gamma (40-150 Hz) and alpha-beta (10-30 Hz) rhythms implements a dynamic mechanism for predictive processing. Namely, predictions enhance alpha-beta oscillations that suppress gamma activity during the processing of predicted inputs. While this model is supported by animal studies, its validity has not been fully explored within the human brain. The present study addresses this by leveraging human intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings across superior temporal and prefrontal/premotor areas of seven presurgical epilepsy patients during an audiovisual speech paradigm. We calculated iEEG power in the theta, alpha-beta, and high gamma bands during simple auditory deviance, multisensory integration, and a condition where an incongruent visual cue (lip movements) clashed with an auditory stimulus (a syllable), creating audiovisual incongruence that can elicit the McGurk illusion. Results revealed increased high-gamma and decreased alpha-beta power in the superior temporal cortex in response to auditory deviance and the McGurk condition, while frontal areas, despite reflecting a similar decrease in alpha-beta power, did not present this high gamma prediction error signal. Instead, the theta band revealed a strong prediction error signal in the McGurk condition, consistent with theories on the role of theta in reorganizing cortical networks. These results both support and extend existing predictive routing models for human-specific forms of predictive processing.

papers.title: Effect of Preoperative Intranasal Dexmedetomidine on Postoperative Myocardial Injury in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the effects of preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine on postoperative myocardial injury biomarkers in patients undergoing on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 70 patients undergoing on-pump CABG were assigned to receive intranasal dexmedetomidine (1 μg/kg) or saline 30 min before bedtime on the night before surgery and again 30 min before anesthesia induction. The primary outcome was serum high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) at 24 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes included perioperative cardiac biomarkers, preoperative sleep quality, postoperative delirium, and adverse events. For the prespecified primary outcome, hs-cTnT concentrations at 24 h after surgery were significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group than in the control group (estimated marginal means, 170.29 vs 357.29 ng/L; P < 0.001). Postoperative creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) concentrations were also lower in the dexmedetomidine group (all P < 0.05). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide showed a significant group-by-time interaction (P = 0.030), although between-group differences at individual postoperative time points were not significant. The dexmedetomidine group had higher Leeds Sleep Evaluation Questionnaire scores (62 [60-64] vs 44 [41-50]; P < 0.001) and a lower incidence of postoperative delirium (14.3% vs 37.1%; P = 0.029). Adverse events, mechanical ventilation duration, and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay did not differ significantly between groups. In this single-center trial, two-dose preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine was associated with lower postoperative hs-cTnT and CK-MB concentrations, better subjective preoperative sleep quality, and a lower observed incidence of postoperative delirium. These findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered multicenter randomized trials to determine whether the biomarker reductions translate into clinically meaningful cardiovascular benefits. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500111431.

papers.title: Psychological support for depression and anxiety across chronic illness contexts: a comparative evaluation of three general-purpose AI chatbots.
papers.abstract: Digital mental health tools, including general-purpose artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots, may provide accessible and low-threshold psychological support for people living with chronic conditions. However, their value in this population depends not only on recognizing depression or anxiety, but also on understanding how psychological distress is shaped by disease-specific experiences and when self-guided support should transition toward professional care. We evaluated the appropriateness, contextual sensitivity, safety, and consistency of psychological support provided by three widely accessible AI chatbots across contrasting chronic illness contexts. We conducted a standardized simulated-patient benchmarking study comparing ChatGPT, Gemini, and Doubao. Twenty scenarios were developed across type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU), representing matched mild and moderate presentations of depression and anxiety together with condition-specific distress related to diabetes self-management and CSU-related flare uncertainty. Each scenario was independently submitted to all three systems in two testing rounds, yielding 120 responses. Blinded raters assessed overall psychological support appropriateness, recognition and emotional support, chronic-illness contextualization, psychological support and referral, psychosomatic balance and safety, and major clinical or safety errors. Repeated testing assessed response consistency. Overall psychological support appropriateness differed across systems (P = 0.002), with 90.0% of ChatGPT, 75.0% of Gemini, and 55.0% of Doubao responses meeting the prespecified appropriateness threshold. Recognition and emotional support was consistently strong across systems, whereas greater differences emerged in chronic-illness contextualization (P = 0.001), psychological support and referral (P = 0.002), and psychosomatic balance and safety (P<0.001). All responses to mild presentations were classified as psychologically appropriate, compared with 58.3% of responses to moderate presentations, indicating that performance became less reliable when digital support required stronger escalation toward professional assessment. Contextualization was also less consistent in CSU, particularly when responses needed to incorporate flare unpredictability, pruritus, sleep disruption, and illness uncertainty. Major clinical or safety errors occurred in 0%, 10.0%, and 15.0% of first-round ChatGPT, Gemini, and Doubao responses, respectively. Test-retest consistency was moderate and varied between systems. General-purpose AI chatbots show potential as accessible, self-guided digital mental health resources for people living with chronic conditions, particularly for recognizing distress and providing initial supportive guidance. Their current limitations emerge when effective support requires disease-specific contextualization, balanced interpretation of psychological and somatic factors, or escalation as symptoms become more severe. These findings identify important boundaries for the use of conversational AI in chronic-illness mental health care and suggest that implementation should emphasize context-sensitive guidance, severity-responsive referral, and clear integration with rather than substitution for professional care.

papers.title: Nocturnal sleep duration, clinical activity score, and thyroid functional remission after radioactive iodine therapy in Graves' disease with thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy.
papers.abstract: To examine whether pretreatment nocturnal sleep duration and Clinical Activity Score (CAS) are associated with thyroid functional remission after radioactive iodine (¹³¹I) therapy in Graves' disease (GD) with concomitant thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy (TAO). The primary endpoint was thyroid functional remission, not ocular cure. We retrospectively reviewed 153 patients at a single center (53 in remission; 100 not in remission), followed for at least 12 months after ¹³¹I therapy. Sleep duration and CAS were pretreatment baseline measures; 20 patients received prednisone before ¹³¹I therapy (discontinued ≥ 3 days prior) and 133 received none; no thyroid-directed or immunosuppressive treatment was given during follow-up. Remission was coded using the response categories of the 2021 Chinese Society of Nuclear Medicine ¹³¹I treatment guideline (euthyroidism or hypothyroidism vs. partial or ineffective response). Missing continuous values were multiply imputed (20 chains). Analyses included false discovery rate (FDR)-controlled univariate screening, cross-validated least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) selection, post-selection logistic regression, Firth sensitivity analysis, interaction tests, and mutually adjusted restricted cubic splines (RCS). No patient sleeping less than 6h achieved remission [0/31; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0%-9.2%]. After FDR adjustment, GD duration, TAO duration, sleep duration, and CAS remained associated with remission. LASSO (one-standard-error rule, C = 0.142) retained GD duration, sleep duration, and CAS. In the post-selection model, the odds ratio (OR) per month of GD duration was 0.991 (95% CI 0.979-1.003; P = 0.152); per additional sleep hour, 6.13 (95% CI 3.16-11.91; P < 0.001; Firth OR 5.64, 95% CI 2.99-10.63); and per CAS point, 0.64 (95% CI 0.48-0.86; P = 0.003). The CAS × sleep interaction was not significant (Wald P = 0.096; likelihood-ratio P = 0.086). Mutually adjusted RCS supported non-linearity for CAS (P < 0.001) but not for sleep (P = 0.585). Longer pretreatment nocturnal sleep and lower CAS were associated with thyroid functional remission after ¹³¹I therapy in this single-center cohort, with consistent directions across sensitivity models. These retrospective, post-selection associations require prospective validation; the absence of remission below 6h and the fitted threshold effects are exploratory post hoc observations, not validated thresholds.

papers.title: The Moderating Effect of Sleep Duration on the Association Between Chronic Disease and Health-Related Quality of Life in Middle-Aged Women.
papers.abstract: This cross-sectional secondary data analysis aimed to examine the association between the number of chronic diseases and health-related quality of life (HRQOL) in middle-aged women and to determine whether sleep duration moderated this association. Data from 3062 women aged 46-70 years were obtained from the 2019 and 2021 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Surveys. Complex-samples t-tests, analysis of variance, and multiple regression analyses were conducted. A significant moderating effect of sleep duration was observed for the > 9 h/day group compared with the > 6-7 h/day reference group (p = 0.016), with a stronger negative association between the number of chronic diseases and HRQOL in this group. Participants in the > 6-7 h/day and > 7-8 h/day groups reported significantly higher HRQOL than those sleeping ≤ 5, > 8-9, and > 9 h/day (p < 0.001), and a greater number of chronic diseases was associated with lower HRQOL (p < 0.001). These findings suggest that sleep duration, particularly sleep duration of more than 9 h, may be considered when evaluating the association between the number of chronic diseases and HRQOL among middle-aged women.

papers.title: Effectiveness Evaluation and Predictive Model Construction of Multi-modal Intervention Program Based on Psychological Resilience Theory in Perioperative Anxiety Management for Cataract Surgery.
papers.abstract: To investigate the effectiveness of a multi-modal intervention program based on psychological resilience theory in perioperative anxiety management for cataract surgery and to establish an anxiety risk prediction model. A prospective randomized controlled trial was conducted, including 120 patients who underwent phacoemulsification with intraocular lens implantation in the ophthalmology department of the hospital from March 2024 to March 2025. Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention group (n=63) and a control group (n=57). The control group received routine perioperative care, while the intervention group received a psychological resilience theory-based intervention program in addition to routine care. The primary outcome measure was the change in State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) state anxiety scores. Secondary outcome measures included Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC-25) scores, Generalized Anxiety Disorder Scale (GAD-7) scores, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), physiological indicators (blood pressure, heart rate), Visual Analog Scale (VAS) pain scores, surgical cooperation scores, and postoperative complication rates. Multiple stepwise regression analysis was used to construct an anxiety risk prediction model, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was employed to evaluate the model's predictive performance. No statistically significant differences were found in baseline characteristics between the 2 groups (all P > .05). The intervention group demonstrated significantly greater reductions in STAI state anxiety scores compared to the control group at all follow-up time points. At 1 month postoperatively, the intervention group achieved a mean reduction of 16.6 ± 8.9 points compared to 9.6 ± 7.2 points in the control group (mean difference=7.0, 95% CI: 3.9-10.1, P < .001). The intervention group showed significantly greater improvements in CD-RISC-25 scores at 1-month follow-up compared to the control group (mean increase: 16.1 ± 9.8 vs. 3.6 ± 8.2 points, P < .001). The GAD-7 and PSQI scores showed significantly greater reductions in the intervention group at all postoperative time points (all P < .001). At 30 minutes preoperatively, the intervention group showed significantly lower systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and heart rate compared to the control group (127.8 ± 13.2 vs. 137.4 ± 16.1 mmHg, 77.9 ± 9.4 vs. 84.2 ± 11.3 mmHg, 74.2 ± 10.8 vs. 86.7 ± 13.4 beats/min, respectively, all P ≤ .001). The intervention group demonstrated significantly lower VAS pain scores at all postoperative time points, higher surgical cooperation scores (4.3 ± 0.8 vs. 3.6 ± 0.9, P < .001), shorter time to first ambulation (7.2 ± 2.4 vs. 9.8 ± 3.1 hours, P < .001), and reduced length of stay (2.3 ± 0.7 vs. 2.9 ± 0.9 days, P < .001). The total incidence of postoperative complications was significantly lower in the intervention group compared to the control group (28.6% vs. 56.1%, P=.003). The constructed anxiety risk prediction model included 7 predictive factors: age, gender, education level, previous surgical history, baseline blood pressure, baseline psychological resilience level, and social support score. The model demonstrated good fit (R 2=0.689, adjusted R 2=0.671), with an area under the ROC curve of 0.863 (95% CI: 0.802-0.924), sensitivity of 84.2%, and specificity of 81.4%. The multi-modal intervention program based on psychological resilience theory effectively reduces perioperative anxiety levels in cataract patients, enhances psychological resilience, improves physiological indicators, alleviates postoperative pain, increases surgical cooperation, shortens recovery time, and reduces complication rates. The constructed anxiety risk prediction model demonstrates good predictive performance.

papers.title: Avoiding Diagnostic Pitfalls in Facial Pain: A Case Report of Paroxysmal Hemicrania Initially Treated as Trigeminal Neuralgia.
papers.abstract: A 21-year-old man presented with a two-year history of recurrent, strictly unilateral left-sided pain in the upper maxillary and orbital regions, radiating to the temporal and occipital areas. Individual attacks lasted 20 to 30 minutes and occurred 10 to 20 times daily, on most days throughout the two-year period. He had been diagnosed elsewhere with trigeminal neuralgia and treated with carbamazepine 200 mg twice daily without benefit. He denied photophobia, phonophobia, and ipsilateral cranial autonomic features, but described prominent restlessness during attacks. No cutaneous or mucosal trigger could be identified, and neurological examination was normal. The attack duration, the reported high attack frequency, the absence of tactile triggers, and the restlessness were inconsistent with classical trigeminal neuralgia and raised suspicion of a trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia, including probable paroxysmal hemicrania. Carbamazepine was withdrawn, and an escalating oral indomethacin trial was initiated, reaching 225 mg daily and maintained at that dose for 14 consecutive days. A headache diary begun on the first day of the trial recorded headache on all 20 days, and the patient reported no improvement at any point. Because the phenotype fulfilled all but the indomethacin-response criterion, the diagnosis was recorded as probable paroxysmal hemicrania, while cluster headache and other trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias remained in the differential diagnosis. Verapamil 240 mg daily was substituted on day 21. Headache days fell to 23 of 31 in the first month and 13 of 31 in the second, with the last 18 days of the second month free of headache. At telephone follow-up, the patient reported sustained resolution, with only mild headaches related to sleep deprivation that he considered distinct from his previous syndrome. He remains on verapamil. Whether verapamil produced the improvement cannot be established from a single uncontrolled case, as the drug was never withdrawn, and spontaneous remission remains possible. This case illustrates the clinical overlap between trigeminal neuralgia and the trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias and highlights the value of structured longitudinal symptom recording, ideally including individual attack count, duration, autonomic features, and triggers.

papers.title: The gut microbiota-derived butyrate improves gestational glucose homeostasis through HDAC3 inhibition and epigenetic activation of the SCGN/GLP-1 axis.
papers.abstract: A deficiency in the gut microbiota-derived metabolite butyrate is associated with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), yet the causative molecular pathways remain undefined. Given its established role as a histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor, we hypothesised that butyrate exerts its beneficial effects on gestational glucose homeostasis through epigenetic reprogramming of intestinal hormone secretion. We integrated clinical observation with causal experimentation. First, a nested case-control study measured serum butyrate and active GLP-1 in pregnant women. Second, a GDM mouse model induced by high-fat diet and antibiotics was treated with the butyrate-producing probiotic Clostridium butyricum for metabolic and microbial profiling. Colon tissues were analysed for HDAC expression and histone acetylation. Third, the mechanism was dissected in enteroendocrine cells using sodium butyrate, HDAC3 modulation, and integrated RNA-sequencing/H3K27ac chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing. Finally, HDAC3 heterozygous knockout mice were used for genetic validation. In the clinical cohort, serum butyrate and GLP-1 levels were consistently lower in women who developed GDM, evident both in early and mid-pregnancy (both p < 0.05). In mice, C. butyricum supplementation alleviated hyperglycaemia, insulin resistance, and circadian glucose rhythm disruption. This was paralleled by elevated systemic butyrate, enrichment of butyrate-producing gut bacteria, decreased colonic HDAC3 protein, and increased global histone H3K27 acetylation (H3K27ac). Multi-omics analysis in enteroendocrine cells identified secretagogin (SCGN) as a direct target gene, with butyrate enhancing both its transcription and promoter-associated H3K27ac. Consequently, butyrate and HDAC3 knockdown increased SCGN expression and GLP-1 secretion, whereas HDAC3 overexpression suppressed this axis-an effect reversible by co-treatment with butyrate. The metabolic improvements and SCGN upregulation driven by C. butyricum were abolished in HDAC3-haploinsufficient mice. We demonstrate that butyrate ameliorates GDM by specifically inhibiting intestinal HDAC3. This inhibition epigenetically activates the transcription of SCGN via enhanced H3K27ac, leading to potentiated GLP-1 secretion. Our work delineates a novel gut microbiota-epigenetic-hormonal axis, identifying HDAC3 and the downstream SCGN/GLP-1 pathway as potential targets for the prevention or treatment of GDM.

papers.title: Night Shift Work and Self-Reported Health Problems Among Hospital Workers in Mogadishu, Somalia: A Descriptive Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Night shift work disrupts circadian rhythms and sleep and has been linked to physical, psychological and occupational health problems. Evidence from Somalia, where hospitals operate with severe staff shortages and limited occupational health support, is scarce. To describe night shift work characteristics and the prevalence of self-reported physical, psychological and occupational health problems among hospital workers who work night shifts in Mogadishu, Somalia. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted between January and June 2026 among 300 hospital workers recruited by purposive sampling from randomly selected public and private hospitals in Mogadishu. Nurses, doctors, laboratory staff, midwives, pharmacists and other hospital staff who had worked night shifts for at least six months completed a structured, self-administered questionnaire developed by the research team, in which each health problem was recorded as a single yes/no item. Prevalence is reported with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Most participants worked rotating shifts (60.7%), 68.7% worked night shifts of 12 hours or longer, and 68.0% were dissatisfied with their shift schedule. The most frequently reported problems were stress (78.7%; 95% CI 73.7-82.9), frequent fatigue (76.0%; 70.9-80.5), sleep problems (71.3%; 66.0-76.2), reduced concentration (68.7%; 63.2-73.7), headaches (64.0%; 58.4-69.2), anxiety (62.7%; 57.1-67.9) and burnout symptoms (58.0%; 52.3-63.4), followed by gastrointestinal problems (39.3%; 34.0-45.0), hypertension symptoms (34.0%; 28.9-39.5) and work-related errors during night shifts (30.7%; 25.7-36.1). Self-reported sleep-related, physical, psychological and occupational problems were highly prevalent among night shift hospital workers in Mogadishu. Because the study was descriptive and cross-sectional, with no day-shift comparison group, the findings show the burden of these problems but do not establish that night shift work caused them. Hospital leaders should review shift scheduling and strengthen occupational and mental health support, and longitudinal studies using validated instruments are needed.

papers.title: Association Between Dietary Vitamin Intake and Short Sleep Duration Among Adults in the United States: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of 2021-2023 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) Data.
papers.abstract: Objective Short sleep duration (SSD) and inadequate dietary vitamin intake are both relevant to overall health and may share relationships with chronic disease risk. However, the relationship between dietary vitamin intake and sleep duration remains incompletely characterized, particularly when vitamin intake is evaluated relative to total energy consumption; additionally, limited research has been done to evaluate the relationship between SSD and vitamins that are not traditionally associated with sleep. Understanding these associations may help clarify potential nutritional factors related to sleep duration. This study evaluated associations between SSD and dietary intake of vitamins A, B1, B2, B3, B6, B9, B12, C, D, E, and K per 1,000 kilocalories among adults in the United States. Materials and methods This cross-sectional study used 2021-2023 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) data. Adults aged ≥20 years with complete sleep, dietary, covariate, and Day 1 dietary weight data were included (n=4,169). SSD was defined as fewer than 7 hours of usual weekday/workday sleep. Primary endpoints were vitamins A, B6, and K; all other vitamins were secondary endpoints. Participants were categorized into low, middle, and high intake tertiles for each vitamin. Separate weighted logistic regression models were performed using the NHANES Day 1 dietary sample weight and adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, income-to-poverty ratio, total energy intake, and body mass index. NHANES strata and primary sampling units were not incorporated into the analysis. Results SSD prevalence decreased across low-to-high intake groups for vitamin A (24.2% to 16.4%), vitamin B6 (22.7% to 18.7%), and vitamin K (23.5% to 17.8%). Higher intake remained associated with lower odds of SSD for vitamin A (aOR=0.710, 95% CI 0.710-0.711), vitamin B6 (aOR=0.724, 95% CI 0.723-0.725), and vitamin K (aOR=0.815, 95% CI 0.814-0.816). Weaker inverse associations were observed for vitamins B1, B2, B3, B12, D, and E. Vitamin C demonstrated a nonlinear inverse pattern, whereas vitamin B9 showed a direct association. Conclusion Higher dietary intake of vitamins A, B6, and K was associated with lower odds of SSD among adults in the United States. Causation cannot be inferred because of the cross-sectional study design. In addition, confidence intervals and significance estimates should be interpreted cautiously because NHANES strata and primary sampling units were not incorporated into the analysis. Prospective studies using full complex survey methods are warranted to further evaluate these associations.
